summary: A Curaprox blog article examining whether fluoride toothpaste is harmful. It explains what fluoride is, where it occurs, how it protects enamel against decay through remineralisation, a protective film and antibacterial action, and reviews claimed side effects such as fluorosis, bone fluorosis, toxicity, pregnancy and IQ concerns, pineal gland, thyroid and rash. It concludes fluoride is effective and safe when used properly, weighs zero-fluoride toothpastes against fluoride ones, and promotes Curaprox products. The note is truncated before its final section on who should use zero fluoride toothpaste.
one_line: Curaprox blog article arguing that fluoride toothpaste is effective against dental decay and safe when used properly, weighing it against zero-fluoride alternatives.
key_facts: Since 1850, the protective effects of fluoride-containing tooth enamel against acids have been recognised.
Fluoride has been recommended for protection against dental decay since 1874.
Over 300,000 scientific studies have explored fluoride's role in combating dental decay.
Tap water in Germany is considered low in fluoride, with a value of less than 0.3 mg per litre.
Seawater typically contains fluoride at an average concentration of 1 mg per litre.
The German Nutrition Society (DGE) recommends total fluoride consumption of 3.1 mg per day for women and 3.8 mg per day for men.
Typical dietary fluoride intake is around 0.4 to 0.6 mg per day.
A 2016 German Dental Association study found twice as many caries-free teeth in 2014 as in 1997.
The potentially toxic dose of fluoride is 5 mg per kilogram of body weight.
Fluoride is almost ten times less toxic than table salt, according to the German Dental Association.
The U.S. National Research Council indicated crippling skeletal fluorosis might occur after ingesting 10 to 20 mg of fluoride per day for 10 to 20 years.
A 2017 study by the U.S. National Health Institute and others examined fluoride intake during pregnancy and child IQ, using drinking water in Mexico.
Perioral dermatitis is a red rash around the mouth and chin that primarily affects women aged 16 to 50 and children.
Stiftung Warentest and Öko-Test consider zero fluoride toothpastes less effective in protecting against dental decay.
Curaprox fluoride toothpastes are free from SLS, microplastics and triclosan.
The article notes that rinsing with water after brushing diminishes fluoride's effectiveness, so it is better to just spit out the toothpaste.

entities.role: Conducted a 2016 oral health study and states fluoride is almost ten times less toxic than table salt

entities.role: Determined a child may have an upset tummy at worst after consuming a whole tube of children's toothpaste

entities.name: German Nutrition Society (DGE)
entities.role: Established recommended guide values for total fluoride consumption

entities.name: Max Rubner-Institut (MRI)
entities.role: Provides the Federal Food Key data on fluoride content in foods

entities.name: U.S. National Research Council
entities.role: Issued a report indicating crippling skeletal fluorosis risk at 10 to 20 mg fluoride per day

entities.name: Paracelsus
entities.role: Early modern physician who concluded in the 16th century that the dose makes the poison

entities.name: Fluorosis
entities.role: Overdose condition from excess fluoride causing white spots on teeth, mainly in children

entities.name: Perioral dermatitis
entities.role: Red rash around the mouth and chin, resembling acne, with suspected causes including fluoride toothpaste

entities.name: Fluorapatite
entities.role: Mineral formed when fluoride replaces hydroxide ions in enamel, considerably stronger than hydroxyapatite

entities.name: Hydroxyapatite
entities.role: Mineral making up a large percentage of the foundation of tooth enamel
